model_choice.accepted_scope: Fixture-local composition of constant-geometry scalar-burn MassState evolution with two consecutive FrozenInterval rigid translations and atomic closing-boundary commits.
model_choice.temporal_policy: Interval k integrates with committed mass m_k. Fuel flow produces candidate m_{k+1}, which remains hidden until the closing tick. The rigid and mass candidates commit together, and interval k+1 reads the newly committed rigid state and mass.
model_choice.trajectory_policy: Identity attitude, zero angular rate, zero moment and a held body force aligned with the inertial x axis reduce each interval to exact constant acceleration. The independent reference composes two analytic segments; the C++17 probe uses classical RK4.
model_choice.mass_policy: candidate_mass = committed_mass - nonnegative_rate * interval_duration; CoM and every inertia entry remain exactly constant under MODEL-YYZ-SCALAR-BURN-CONSTANT-GEOMETRY-001.
excluded: aero, environment and propulsion query recomputation inside either interval
fuel geometry, dry mass, depletion events, CoM or inertia motion
configuration changes, canonical mission or vehicle assets
public runtime, transaction or product contracts and R1-R8 capability

model.integration: classical fixed-step RK4 with q_I_B normalization
validity_domain: all identities, ticks and configuration revisions agree
exactly two contiguous one-tick half-open intervals are supplied
base_dt_s is positive and all physical inputs are finite
current and candidate mass are strictly positive and fuel-consumption rates are nonnegative
q_I_B is identity up to sign, angular rate and held moment are zero
CoM is finite and inertia is symmetric positive definite
the terminal tick equals the second closing tick

equivalence_cases.operation: integrate each frozen interval with one full RK4 step and with two half RK4 steps
equivalence_cases.expected: both paths reach the same committed tick-2 rigid and mass state

invalid_input_cases.mutation: change the second interval body frame
change the second interval configuration revision
change the first interval sample tick
start the second interval after a gap
set the first fuel-consumption rate negative
consume the full committed mass in the first interval
set a nonzero initial angular rate

mutation_cases.mutation: integrate interval zero with its pending mass candidate
integrate interval one with the pre-commit mass
commit mass at tick one while reusing the tick-zero rigid state
